title: Unify presubmit lifecycle with dependency taxonomy and lightweight release adapter
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit matrix and dependency handling have drifted across teams. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a declarative presubmit lifecycle manifest that describes staged lanes (fast-feedback, smoke, integration, nightly) and quiet-merge windows; and (2) a dependency taxonomy and a small classifier tool that tags dependencies as direct/runtime/dev/test/doc. Together these enable targeted presubmit runs, smarter caching priming, and safer automated dependency bumps.

What this changes (summary):
- Add .github/presubmit-lifecycle.yaml: canonical, minimal declarative manifest consumed by the CI router. The manifest maps file globs and labels to staged lanes and defines policy for quiet merges and retry budgets.
- Add tools/dep-classifier/: a lightweight Go binary and heuristics (LICENSE-safe, MIT/Apache analysis omitted) that outputs dependency labels into deps.json for each repo snapshot. This is used to decide which lanes run on a dependency-only change.
- CI router changes: small adapter in .github/actions/ci-router/main.js that reads the lifecycle manifest and deps.json to reduce unnecessary full-matrix runs.
- Repo hygiene codemods: scripts/cleanup/update-go-mods.sh and scripts/cleanup/pyproject-fixup.py to perform safe formatting and pin removal after automated bumps. These are idempotent and opt-in.
- Release adapter: .github/actions/release-lifecycle.yml uses the lifecycle manifest to ensure release smoke jobs are gated behind the same quiet-merge policy and that dependency-rollouts can opt into canaries.

Commits (high level):
- commit 1: introduce presubmit-lifecycle manifest and tests (unit parsing + schema)
- commit 2: add dep-classifier tool + README + unit tests for common package heuristics
- commit 3: wire ci-router to the manifest, add feature flag and migration gate (env: CI_LIFECYCLE_V2)
- commit 4: repo hygiene codemods and docs updates, small examples for SDK repos
- commit 5: release automation adapter and CI integration tests, fix flakiness in router tests

Files changed (representative list):
- .github/presubmit-lifecycle.yaml
- .github/actions/ci-router/main.js
- .github/actions/release-lifecycle.yml
- tools/dep-classifier/main.go
- tools/dep-classifier/README.md
- scripts/cleanup/update-go-mods.sh
- scripts/cleanup/pyproject-fixup.py
- docs/ci/presubmit-lifecycle.md
- docs/ci/dependency-taxonomy.md
- redwood-sdk-python/pyproject.toml (example pin removals)
- redwood/BUILD.bazel (small tidy)

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests for manifest schema validation and dep-classifier heuristics.
- Integration test for CI router feature flag that simulates patch containing only dev dependencies; verifies only fast-feedback and docs lanes run.
- CI initially failed on a flaky router test (node 18 environment), retried once; flaky test fixed by increasing the test timeout and stabilizing the mockfs used by the test harness. Final CI run: all checks passing.

Review notes and conversation:
- Ravi Patel (review): "High-level design looks solid. Two asks: (1) show a sample migration path for teams that still expect the old matrix; (2) ensure the dep classifier has an opt-out for monorepos with custom build rules."
- Author (Maya): "Added a migration section and a feature flag (CI_LIFECYCLE_V2=false by default). Dep classifier now supports a .depclass-ignore file per repo to preserve previous behavior."
- Lena Thompson (review): "Please add a short-lived telemetry flag to capture how many PRs would skip full-matrix runs under the new policy."
- Author: "Telemetry flag added; data is exported to CI telemetry with a 90-day retention and opt-out via CI_TELEMETRY=0."
- Diego Alvarez (approval): "Verified the integration tests and smoke runs. Approving for merge once release adapter is exercised in staging."
- Follow-up: Small hotfix commit to release-lifecycle.yml to set proper RBAC bindings for the release job service account after Diego's sign-off.

Migration plan:
- Step 1: Merge behind feature flag. Default behavior unchanged.
- Step 2: Gradually opt-in teams by setting CI_LIFECYCLE_V2=true in their repo-level CI settings; SDK teams will be onboarded by docs + examples.
- Step 3: After 6 weeks of opt-in telemetry showing reduced full-matrix runs with no regressions, flip default and announce.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: misclassification of a runtime dependency as dev-only could skip critical tests. Mitigation: classifier conservative-by-default (assumes runtime if unclear), .depclass-ignore, and automated post-merge audit that flags any regressions in nightly.
- Risk: new manifest parser could introduce stale behavior. Mitigation: strict schema validation, unit tests, and a dry-run mode implemented in the ci-router action.

Release notes: see release_notes field.

Notes for maintainers: The dep-classifier is intentionally small; we expect future improvements to use language-specific heuristics. For now this provides a consistent vocabulary for presubmit policies and a migration path from our existing ad-hoc labels.
release_notes: Introduce declarative presubmit lifecycle manifest and dependency taxonomy. Adds tools/dep-classifier for tagging dependencies and a CI router adapter to reduce unnecessary full-matrix runs. Feature gated behind CI_LIFECYCLE_V2; gradual opt-in migration. Includes repo hygiene codemods and a release adapter for canary rollouts.
notes: Feature gated; default behavior unchanged until teams opt in. Telemetry added for 90 days. Please coordinate with platform team before flipping default.
